title: U-Boot DRAM load map
unit_note: Every address is an offset from the SoC's DRAM base. A slot's absolute address is base + offset.

families.name: MediaTek (MT8183, MT8365, MT8188)
families.ramdisk_stop_note: On MT8188 the audio DSP's memory starts at base + 0x20000000, so the ramdisk slot never grows past it

low_window.label: Firmware and headroom
low_window.note: Secure firmware lives in the first 64 MiB. No load slot starts below 0x04000000.

uboot_top_note: After relocation U-Boot occupies the top of DRAM: its image, a 128 MiB heap, the stack and a framebuffer.

slots.holds: boot.scr, kept mapped while it loads the fdt and the kernel
one device-tree overlay, until it is applied
the device tree, grown by resize and overlays
spare, so the kernel slot starts on a 2 MiB boundary
the kernel booti runs: a raw Image, or a compressed one decompressed back into this slot. 2 MiB-aligned, so an arm64 Image runs in place
the initramfs. Guaranteed to the 512 MiB ceiling; grows with DRAM

nested.holds: decompress buffer: a compressed kernel (at most kernel_comp_size, 64 MiB) sits at the bottom of the kernel slot, decompresses here and is copied back down

amlogic-open.name: Amlogic open firmware: the reserved block

regions.label: Secure firmware
regions.note: trusted firmware and its staging; on S805X / S905X the first 1 MiB is a read-only ROM mirror

regions.label: Secure monitor mailboxes
regions.note: shared buffers between Linux and the secure monitor

regions.label: ramoops
regions.note: pstore: the previous boot's console and crash records survive a reboot

mechanisms.how: USB DFU into RAM (alternates script, fdt, kernel, ramdisk)

mechanisms.note: U-Boot copies the device tree and the initramfs to the top of free memory below itself before starting the kernel

caveat: A saved U-Boot environment replaces these defaults. A board that has one keeps the addresses it saved until the environment is reset.
